_meta.purpose: City-typical defaults for fields the user might not know.
source_standards: Central Ground Water Board (CGWB) state hydrograph data 2022
honesty_disclaimer: These are CITY-TYPICAL educated guesses, not site-specific values.
Real soil + water table vary plot-by-plot, even within the same city.
When using these defaults, checks emit LOW confidence and recommend
site-specific verification (NABL geotech lab + CGWB district report).
If guess would HARD_FAIL a check, it is downgraded to SOFT_WARN per
the user-approved 'don't block on a guess' principle.

soil_notes: Coastal sandy alluvial dominant. Some pockets of soft clay near
marshes (Pallikaranai, Velachery). Compaction critical.
Building near coast (Thiruvanmiyur, Besant Nagar) has saline
groundwater risk affecting concrete durability.
water_table_notes: Highly variable. Coastal areas near monsoon maximum see ground
saturation. North + central Chennai have deeper water table
(8-12m). Check CGWB district report for your ward.

soil_notes: Laterite + weathered rock dominant. Good bearing capacity.
Periphery (Whitefield, Sarjapur) may have soft clay or fill
pockets — verify before deep foundation decisions.
Central Bangalore (Jayanagar, Indiranagar) has weathered rock
near surface — bearing capacity 250-400 kN/m².
water_table_notes: Generally deep. Severe declining trend over 20 years.
South + East Bangalore typically 12-20m. Some areas now >25m.

soil_notes: Decomposed granite + weathered rock dominant. Generally strong.
Some clay pockets in lakebed areas (Hussainsagar perimeter).
Old city has shallow rock — easy strip foundations.
water_table_notes: Deep generally. Cyberabad/Gachibowli has 15-20m. Older areas

soil_notes: Coastal/reclaimed land dominant. Soft clay layers common.
Reclaimed areas (BKC, Lower Parel, Worli) need pile foundations.
Saline groundwater throughout — concrete spec: M30+ with
corrosion-resistant rebar.
Suburban areas (Borivali, Thane) have better-drained soils.
water_table_notes: Very shallow. Monsoon = surface or just below. Basement

soil_notes: Black cotton soil common in many pockets — swells in monsoon,
shrinks in summer (cracks 100-150mm wide). HIGH RISK for shallow
foundations on G+1+ buildings.
Solution: pile foundation, raft + soil replacement, or under-
reamed piles.
Some suburbs (Hinjawadi, Kothrud) have basalt — better.
water_table_notes: Moderate depth. Monsoon brings shallow zones in low-lying areas.

soil_notes: Yamuna alluvial silty clay/sand dominant. Good bearing for
low-rise; pile or raft for G+3+.
Yamuna floodplain areas (Trans-Yamuna) have soft clay — extra
care needed.
South Delhi often has Aravalli quartzite at depth — strong base.
water_table_notes: Deep generally — Delhi part of CGWB-flagged 'critical' zone.
Trans-Yamuna shallower at 10-15m. South Delhi can be 30-40m.
